inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 non-GAAP diluted weighted-average count (659,356,092; 6-K 2026-09-15 reconciliation table), the latest treasury-stock-method diluted figure. Basic shares were 629.7m at 2026-03-31 (20-F FY2025) and 632.3m weighted in Q2-2026 after ~RMB10bn+ of H1-2026 buybacks under the US$5bn Aug-2025 programme. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count. The US$1.5bn 0.75% 2029 convertible (22.7m ADS at ~US$66 conversion) is carried as debt, not shares; it is far out of the money and puttable June 2027.
inputs.cash_definition: Company's own broad definition at 2026-06-30: cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash 56,016 + short-term investments 23,499 + held-to-maturity time deposits and financial products (inside long-term Investments) 21,001 = RMB100,516m (6-K: 'RMB100.5 billion'). Debt = short-term debt and current portion 25,767 + long-term debt 630 = 26,397 (includes US$500m 1.50% 2027 exchangeable notes and US$1.5bn 0.75% 2029 convertible). Operating-lease liabilities (567 non-current + current portion) EXCLUDED: leases are charged inside adjusted EBITDA (treatment B).
inputs.sbc_source: 20-F FY2025 consolidated cash flow statement 'Share-based compensation' RMB2,270m (ties to the adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation add-back). No separate equity-award tax-withholding line exists: awards are options settled by exercise (proceeds RMB493m in financing), so the combined figure equals the add-back.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity outflow 'Cash paid for repurchasing of ordinary shares' RMB4,396m (20-F). Pace stepped up sharply in H1-2026 under the US$5bn Aug-2025 authorization: basic weighted shares fell 655.9m (Q4-25) -> 649.0m (Q1-26) -> 632.3m (Q2-26), implying ~RMB10bn+ repurchased in H1-2026 (no cash flow statement in the 6-K). Flat count is being FUNDED by repurchases; buybacks are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); ADS (1 ADS = 1 ordinary share) quoted in USD on Nasdaq. fx_rate is the engine's reporting->quote multiplier: 1 CNY = US$0.14915, i.e. USDCNY 6.7048 (Yahoo CNY=X, 2026-10-04T03:30Z). Company's own translation rate at 2026-06-30 was USD1 = RMB6.7851 (Fed certified). Parity check via the HKEX dual listing: 9961.HK HK$302.40 (2026-10-02 close) / USDHKD 7.8463 = US$38.54, within 1.2% of the Nasdaq regular close at inputs.price_as_of the same day -- a tie that confirms direction and quote basis. Note scripts/sanity_check.py uses the reciprocal convention (quote->reporting, 6.7048) for its historical table -- see memory note sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-conflict. Per-share values in CNY are emitted as the *_cny twins.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:01Z regular close (Friday); 52-week range 38.01-78.99, price sits at the bottom of the range
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the flows' currency: 10y CGB risk-free ~1.8% + beta 1.2 x (mature-market ERP 5.0% + China country risk premium ~1.8%) = ~10.0% cost of equity; ~95% equity weight, ~2% after-tax cost of debt -> WACC ~9.6%, rounded up to 10.0%. The country premium is the only China charge in the rate; VIE/antitrust/HFCAA risk is charged ONCE, in the flows, via the 30% bear weight and the bear driver path -- no per-scenario WACC differences. House US-tech default is 10.5% against a 4.2% rf; a 10.0% CNY rate against a 1.8% rf is a wider risk spread.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. US GAAP ASC 842 operating-lease expense (RMB250m ROU amortisation + lease interest) sits inside operating expenses and the company's adjusted EBITDA does NOT add it back (its D&A add-back of 845 = 647 PP&E depreciation + 198 intangibles/land-use amortisation, excluding ROU). Lease liabilities therefore excluded from net debt; da_pct_path is ex-ROU. Charged exactly once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows (NCI share of profit is RMB92m FY2025, ~0.3% of net income, immaterial to the margin path); NCI RMB1,615m + mezzanine redeemable NCI RMB140m at 2026-06-30 deducted ONCE in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1-2: consumer-internet marketplace, non-US filer with reporting currency != quote currency -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md parts a, b, c, d). First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry). OWNER FCF FY2025: reported FCF 13,582 (OCF 14,379 - capex 797) - SBC 2,270 - interest income 2,603 = 8,709. Interest income stripped because net cash RMB74bn is ~8x the FCF base. FY2025 reported FCF is itself depressed by the RMB2,073m capital-gains tax paid on the MakeMyTrip share sale (one-off, in OCF via cash taxes 5,740 vs 2,700 FY2024) and a RMB-5.7bn working-capital outflow (prepayments/other current assets); the component build does not carry that forward. FY0/Y1 TIMING: FY0 = FY2025 actuals (calendar year), Y1 = FY2026, the guidance year; balance sheet is 2026-06-30, so H1-2026 owner FCF (~RMB4-5bn, ~US$1/share) is both in net cash and in the Y1 flow -- partly offset by discounting a 3/4-earned year a full period. Known, stated, not adjusted. FY2026 BASE: H1-2026 revenue 31,871 (+11.2% YoY), Q2 +6% within the 3-8% guide; H2 modelled at ~+4% (SAMR contra-revenue, exclusivity unwind, energy-price headwind on ticketing) -> FY2026E ~66,950, +7%. SAMR: RMB5,180m penalty accrued in Q2-2026 G&A; other current liabilities rose 4.25bn QoQ, so it is treated as accrued-unpaid at 2026-06-30 and deducted in the equity bridge. If any portion was already paid by June 30 the deduction is slightly double -- conservative. GROWTH-DIVERGENCE: historical CAGRs from FY2020-22 bases are COVID artefacts (3y revenue CAGR 46%); the pre-COVID FY2019->FY2025 6y CAGR of 9.8% is the meaningful history and the selected 7% is below it. TERMINAL CAP 15x (not 20x): discretionary travel, China platform regulation. SBC is projected as % of revenue (4.0% anchored to H1-2026's 4.2%, declining to 3.0%). Street basis adds back SBC; band_position reported.

equity_bridge.item: Long-term investments ex HTM deposits (equity-method and fair-value stakes: MakeMyTrip residual, Tongcheng-Elong, H World, BTG etc.) at 80% of book
equity_bridge.note: Investments 51,361 less 21,001 HTM time deposits already in cash = 30,360 book at 2026-06-30 (6-K balance sheet). Their income (equity in affiliates, dividends, fair-value changes) is outside adjusted EBITDA, so the matching-asset rule puts the asset in the bridge. 20% haircut for disposal tax leakage (FY2025 MMYT sale bore ~14% tax) and unlisted-stake discount. The H World stake backs the US$500m exchangeable notes, which are in total_debt.

equity_bridge.item: SAMR anti-monopoly penalty accrued, unpaid at 2026-06-30
equity_bridge.note: RMB5,180m charged to Q2-2026 G&A (6-K 2026-09-15); other current liabilities +4,251 QoQ. Includes RMB1,658m disgorgement and RMB122m hotel-deposit refunds.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests and mezzanine redeemable NCI
equity_bridge.note: 1,615 + 140 at 2026-06-30 (6-K balance sheet); flows are consolidated so the NCI stock is deducted once here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance-anchored (H1 +11%, Q2 guide +3-8% realised +6%, H2 ~+4%); cross-checked against the FY2019->FY2025 pre-COVID revenue CAGR of 9.8% and equity 5y CAGR 11.2%, both above the selected rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3y and 5y CAGRs are computed off COVID-depressed bases (FY2020 revenue 18.3bn vs 35.7bn FY2019) and are not usable: revenue 3y 46% vs equity 3y 15% diverges >30%. EPS and FCF CAGRs are null because FY2020-22 owner FCF and FY2020-21 EPS were negative. Owner FCF grew faster than reported FCF since FY2019 (21.5% vs 13.0%) because SBC (1,714 -> 2,270) and interest income (2,094 -> 2,603) grew slower than FCF; SBC is not eating the growth here, unlike the US SaaS pattern.
historical_growth.notes: FY2025 net income 33,386 includes a RMB19.9bn one-off investment gain (RMB15.2bn MakeMyTrip sale); FY2025 reported FCF carries the RMB2,073m tax on it. Neither is a base.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 FY2026 +7%: H1 actual +11.2%, H2 ~+4% as the SAMR contra-revenue and exclusivity unwind bite and ticketing (-1% in Q2) stays soft. FY2027-29 7-8%: domestic low-single-digit post-remedy, international platform (+50% in Q2-2026, est. low-teens % of revenue) and inbound (high double-digit) contribute ~5-6pp of group growth; decelerates to 3% by Y10 as international matures.
base.margin_rationale: Adj. EBITDA margin 30.3% FY2025, 32% FY2024, 29.5% H1-2026, 29% Q2-2026 with S&M at 25% of revenue amid the competitive/compliance reset. Base holds 29% for two years then drifts to 31% as the loss-making international platform scales; never regains the FY2024 32% peak.
base.tax_rationale: PRC statutory 25%, key subsidiaries at 15% high-tech rate, plus 5-10% withholding on cash repatriated for buybacks. FY2024 GAAP tax / operating income = 18%; FY2025 cash tax ex the RMB2,073m one-off = 3,667 on 15,773 operating income = 23%. SBC is not tax-deductible so the engine's post-SBC EBIT base understates taxable income: 21% on post-SBC EBIT ~ 18% pre-SBC. Flat 21%.
base.wc_rationale: Advances from customers (20.9bn) and payables (20.0bn) roughly match receivables (17.1bn) plus prepayments (25.9bn); FY2024 captured +38% of revenue growth, FY2025 -63% (prepayments/loans-to-users build). Mixed sign -> small 5% capture.

bull.growth_rationale: Domestic recovers to high-single-digit once the remedy is absorbed and the anti-involution campaign hits Meituan/Fliggy equally; international platform sustains 40%+ and inbound compounds toward the 200m-traveller ambition; outbound keeps running >140% of 2019.
bull.margin_rationale: Margin recovers past the FY2024 32% peak to 33.5% as international reaches scale and AI cuts service cost; S&M intensity normalises to ~22%.

bear.growth_rationale: Y1 +5% (H1 already banked at +11%, H2 flat); FY2027-28 +2% as the end of exclusivity and lowest-price clauses compresses accommodation take-rate and Meituan's super-app bundling takes share in a price war; macro (energy, property-sector consumer) caps domestic; international decelerates to 20-25% against Booking/Agoda.
bear.margin_rationale: Take-rate compression and sustained S&M at 28-29% push adj. EBITDA margin to 24%, the FY2023 level, and it stays there; SBC % drifts up as revenue stalls.

scenario_narratives.base: The SAMR remedy (no exclusivity, no lowest-price clauses, refunded deposits) is a one-time reset of domestic take-rate and growth rather than a structural collapse: domestic accommodation and ticketing grow low-single-digit from FY2026, while the Trip.com international platform (+50% YoY) and inbound travel (high double-digit) keep the group at 7-8% through FY2029 before decelerating to 3%. Adjusted EBITDA margin sits at 29% for two years and drifts to 31% as international scales, never regaining the FY2024 32% peak. SBC is charged at 4% of revenue declining to 3%. The RMB74bn net cash and the ~RMB24bn investment portfolio are added at the bridge; the RMB5.2bn fine is deducted. No further antitrust action, and the VIE structure holds.
scenario_narratives.bull: Beijing's anti-involution campaign bites rivals as hard as Trip.com, the remedy normalises the whole OTA market instead of singling out the leader, and domestic growth recovers to high-single-digit. International sustains 40%+ growth and reaches margin breakeven, inbound compounds toward the 200m-traveller target, outbound holds above 140% of 2019. Group growth 11-12% in FY2027-28, adjusted EBITDA margin to 33.5%, terminal growth 3%. The US$5bn buyback at a 5x EV/EBITDA entry point adds to per-share value but is value-neutral in the model.
scenario_narratives.bear: The remedy is not one-and-done: regulators keep pressing dominant platforms, the loss of exclusivity compresses accommodation take-rate, Meituan's bundling triggers a price war, and consumer travel spend stalls on energy prices and the property-sector overhang. Group growth 2-3% from FY2027, adjusted EBITDA margin falls to 24% (the FY2023 level) and stays there, SBC % drifts up. International decelerates to 20-25% against Booking/Agoda. Net cash and investments still floor the value well above zero -- this bear is a stagnant cash box, not a solvency case. The VIE/HFCAA binary tail (contract invalidation, forced delisting without an HK migration) is not modelled as a cash flow; it is the reason the bear weight is 30%, not 15%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: single-regulator dependency (SAMR has just fined the company RMB5.2bn and ordered a change to the core hotel-contract model), a VIE-structured China ADR with a binary legal tail, and management's own linkage of the growth collapse (+17% to +6% in one quarter) to compliance adjustments. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right -- domestic recovery, international reaching scale against Booking/Agoda, and no further regulatory action. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Trip.com is valued as an operating cash-flow stream in RMB on a strict owner-FCF basis (SBC expensed, interest income stripped, share count flat), discounted at a CNY-built 10% WACC, with the RMB74bn broad net cash, the investment portfolio at 80% of book, the accrued SAMR fine and NCI bridged to equity, then translated to USD per ADS at the live rate. The three scenarios are the axes the Analysis JSON identifies: durability of the domestic take-rate after the antitrust remedy, the pace of the international/inbound build-out, and whether platform regulation recurs. Risk is charged once -- in the flows and the 30% bear weight -- not stacked into the discount rate. Terminal value is capped at 15x owner FCF because travel is discretionary and the regulatory regime is restrictive.
key_risks_to_valuation: Recurring PRC platform antitrust action or a sector-wide price war compressing accommodation take-rate below the bear path
VIE contractual-structure invalidation or HFCAA-driven Nasdaq delisting (HK listing mitigates liquidity, not VIE risk) -- a binary tail outside the cash-flow model
RMB depreciation versus USD: every 5% move in USDCNY moves the USD per-ADS value ~5% with no change in the RMB business
The investment portfolio (RMB30bn book) is added at 80% of book; listed stakes could trade below carrying value and unlisted stakes could be impaired
H1-2026 owner FCF (~RMB4-5bn) is counted in both the June-30 net cash and the FY2026 Y1 flow (~US$1/share overstatement, partly offset by full-period discounting of a 3/4-earned year)
Travel demand shock (pandemic, geopolitics, energy) -- FY2020 showed owner FCF can swing to -RMB8bn in a year
